Chapter 1


1       The tidiest town




In Fairhollow, nobody ever cried at the cinema, because there was
nothing sad to see. Every song and story went to the Calm Office first. The
Office edited them, taking out storms, goodbyes and angry words.
Even the river was tidy. Every Monday, workers cut its reeds, so the water
lay flat and still like glass.
That spring, Nora’s school sent her to help at the Calm Office after school.
‘You will keep people happy,’ said her mother proudly.
Nora felt proud too. She liked things neat. She did not know yet what neat
could cost.


Read and circle
What did workers do to the river every Monday?

           A. They cut its reeds.

           B. They cleaned its fish.

           C. They built a new bridge.

2 · Think about it
What does ‘She did not know yet what neat could cost’ suggest?

           A. Nora will soon want to leave her job at the Office.

           B. Nora will have to pay to work there.

           C. Keeping things neat has a hidden price.



3 · Write it
Would you like to live in a town with nothing sad in it? What might be missing?
